nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Microfiltration systems_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How was the surface area and pore size distribution of the samples determined?
nodes.answer: The surface area and pore size distribution were determined by nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm using the Quantochrome Autosorp device.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Microfiltration systems_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does micro-XCT differ from standard XCT?
nodes.answer: Micro-XCT provides sub-millimeter and even sub-micron XCT to examine the physical properties and morphological composition of samples, whereas standard XCT may not achieve this level of resolution.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Microfiltration systems_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What volume of filtered seawater was used in the incubation chambers for symbiont sampling?
nodes.answer: A volume of 150 mL of 0.2 m filtered seawater was used in the incubation chambers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Microfiltration systems_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How was the pure Pb(NO3)2 solution obtained from the initial mixture?
nodes.answer: The pure Pb(NO3)2 solution was obtained by filtration through a 0.22 m filter.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Microfiltration systems_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What equipment was used for the peptide separation process?
nodes.answer: The peptide mixture was separated using a NanoACQUITY UPLC MClass system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Microfiltration systems_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What particles predominantly pass through wet scrubbers and what is their size range?
nodes.answer: Particles in the size range of 60-200 nm predominantly pass through wet scrubbers, constituting a significant portion of the inhalable particle mass.
